name: Intelligent Payment Routing
tagline: Build a routing policy that survives conditions it has never seen.
narrative: You have joined YamusaPay's Payments Infrastructure team. The switch receives consumer, business, refund, and international transfers while provider availability, capacity, latency, fees, and reliability change. Every route occupies a provider slot until processing completes. Failed attempts may be retried, but retries consume deadline budget and increase cost. The visible stream teaches the contract; submission runs the same policy against hidden outages, capacity exhaustion, fee changes, latency spikes, and late high-value traffic.
objective: Process the visible stream without timeouts, protect urgent and high-value payments, and submit a policy that generalizes across all hidden scenarios.
learningObjective: Combine availability, compatibility, capacity, reliability, cost, urgency, and retry history in one ordered routing policy.
intelligenceExplanation: The interview starts with no routing rules. Build the policy from the operational contract: filter eligibility and capacity first, then express reliability, urgency, retry, and cost preferences as guarded branches. A provider being online does not mean it can accept the current payment.
hint: Start with the non-negotiable constraints: canRoute, deadline, priority, and supported value/type. Only compare cost after those filters.
hints: Separate eligibility from preference. Use canRouteA/B/C before fee or expected cost.
Reserve the most reliable, low-latency route for urgent or high-value payments, and avoid immediately repeating a failed provider.
A robust fallback ends in hold only when the deadline permits waiting; otherwise choose an eligible route or decline deliberately.
brief: Author and submit a resilient payment-routing policy against one visible and six hidden real-time scenarios.
context: One tick is one routing decision while providers continue processing previously routed payments in parallel.
